meta.description: Display the full details of a single credit card transaction retrieved from the TRANSACT file by Transaction ID.
meta.process_description: This program allows a bank operator or customer service representative to look up and view the complete details of a specific credit card transaction by entering its Transaction ID. Upon receiving a valid Transaction ID, the program retrieves the transaction record from the TRANSACT file and displays all associated details including the card number, transaction type, category, source, amount, description, origination and processing timestamps, and merchant information (ID, name, city, ZIP code). The program is typically invoked from the transaction list screen (COTRN00C), where a specific transaction has been selected, and supports navigation back to the calling screen or to the transaction list. If the Transaction ID is not found or is left blank, appropriate error messages are displayed to the user.

files.TRANSACT: Master file storing all credit card transaction records, keyed by Transaction ID

business_rules: Transaction ID is mandatory; the system will not attempt a lookup and will display an error message if the field is left blank.
If the entered Transaction ID does not exist in the TRANSACT file, the user is informed with a 'Transaction ID NOT found' message and no transaction details are displayed.
When navigated from the transaction list screen (COTRN00C), the selected Transaction ID is automatically populated and the lookup is performed without requiring manual entry.
The program reads the transaction record with an UPDATE intent (CICS READ UPDATE), suggesting the record may be locked for potential downstream editing, even though this screen is view-only.

Navigation via PF3 returns the user to the originating program (or the main menu if no originating program is recorded); PF5 returns directly to the transaction list screen (COTRN00C); PF4 clears all fields on the current screen.
Any unrecognised key press is rejected with an 'invalid key' message, enforcing controlled navigation.

If the program is accessed without a valid communication area (e.g., direct access without prior sign-on), the user is redirected to the sign-on screen (COSGN00C), enforcing authentication requirements.

variables.name: WS-VARIABLES
variables.description: Top-level working storage group holding all internal program control variables used during transaction detail retrieval and display processing.

variables.name: WS-PGMNAME
variables.description: The internal name of this program (COTRN01C), used when invoking CICS services such as returning control or logging, so the system knows which program is currently executing.

variables.name: WS-TRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction identifier (CT01) assigned to this transaction detail view program. It is used when transferring control back to this screen, ensuring the correct screen is invoked within the CardDemo application.

variables.name: WS-MESSAGE
variables.description: The status or error message displayed to the user at the bottom of the transaction detail screen — for example, 'Transaction ID NOT found' when a lookup fails, or 'Invalid key pressed' for unrecognised navigation keys.

variables.name: WS-TRANSACT-FILE
variables.description: The name of the master transaction file (TRANSACT) that stores all credit card transaction records. This value is used when issuing CICS file read commands to retrieve a specific transaction by its Transaction ID.

variables.name: WS-ERR-FLG
variables.description: An internal error indicator that tracks whether a business or system error has occurred during transaction lookup or screen processing. When set to 'Y', it prevents further processing and ensures the error message is shown to the user instead of transaction details.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-ON
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when an error has been detected during transaction processing — such as a missing Transaction ID or a failed file lookup — signalling that normal display logic should be bypassed.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-OFF
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when no error has occurred, indicating that the transaction lookup was successful and the full transaction details can be safely displayed to the user.

variables.name: WS-RESP-CD
variables.description: The CICS response code returned after a file operation (such as reading the TRANSACT file). A non-zero value indicates a problem — for example, a record not found or a file unavailability — which triggers an appropriate error message to the user.

variables.name: WS-REAS-CD
variables.description: The CICS reason code accompanying the response code, providing additional detail about why a file operation failed. Used alongside WS-RESP-CD to diagnose specific error conditions when retrieving a transaction record.

variables.name: WS-USR-MODIFIED
variables.description: A flag indicating whether the user has manually changed any field on the transaction detail screen. This helps the program distinguish between an initial display pass and a user-driven interaction requiring re-processing.

variables.name: USR-MODIFIED-YES
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when the user has actively modified a field on the screen, such as entering or changing a Transaction ID, indicating that the program should act on the new input.

variables.name: USR-MODIFIED-NO
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when the user has not changed any field on the screen, indicating the display is in its initial or unchanged state and no new lookup is required.

variables.name: WS-TRAN-AMT
variables.description: The formatted monetary amount of the credit card transaction, displayed on screen with a sign indicator and two decimal places. This represents the dollar value charged or credited in the transaction, formatted for human-readable presentation.

variables.name: WS-TRAN-DATE
variables.description: A formatted date field used to display the transaction date (either origination or processing date) on the screen in MM/DD/YY format, making the transaction timeline clear to the user.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT01-INFO
variables.description: A group of fields passed via the communication area from the transaction list screen (COTRN00C) to this detail view program, carrying context about which transaction was selected and the pagination state of the list the user came from.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT01-TRNID-FIRST
variables.description: The Transaction ID of the first transaction displayed on the transaction list screen the user navigated from. Retained so that if the user returns to the list, the correct page position can be restored.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT01-TRNID-LAST
variables.description: The Transaction ID of the last transaction displayed on the transaction list screen the user navigated from. Used together with CDEMO-CT01-TRNID-FIRST to restore the correct page of results when the user navigates back.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT01-PAGE-NUM
variables.description: The page number of the transaction list the user was viewing before drilling into this transaction detail screen. Preserved so the user is returned to the same page of results when pressing PF3 or PF5 to go back.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT01-NEXT-PAGE-FLG
variables.description: A flag indicating whether there are more pages of transactions available beyond the current page in the transaction list. Carried across to preserve the navigation state of the list screen when the user returns.

variables.name: NEXT-PAGE-YES
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when additional pages of transaction records exist beyond the current page in the transaction list, enabling forward pagination when the user returns to the list.

variables.name: NEXT-PAGE-NO
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when no further pages of transactions exist beyond the current page, indicating the user has reached the end of the transaction list.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT01-TRN-SEL-FLG
variables.description: A flag passed from the transaction list screen indicating whether the user has actively selected a specific transaction for detail viewing. When set, it signals this program to automatically perform the transaction lookup without requiring manual entry.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT01-TRN-SELECTED
variables.description: The Transaction ID chosen by the user on the transaction list screen (COTRN00C), passed to this program so that the correct transaction record is automatically retrieved and displayed without requiring the user to re-enter the ID manually.

variables.name: DFHCOMMAREA
variables.description: The CICS communication area received by this program when it is invoked. It carries session context — such as user identity, originating program, and selected transaction — from the previous screen, enabling the program to authenticate the user and pre-populate the transaction lookup.

variables.name: LK-COMMAREA
variables.description: A minimal placeholder representing the raw communication area data passed into this program by CICS. Its presence (or absence) is checked to determine whether the user arrived via a proper authenticated navigation path; if absent, the user is redirected to the sign-on screen.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.description: MAIN-PARA is the central orchestration routine of the transaction detail viewer. It determines the user's context and intent — whether they are arriving for the first time, returning after an action, or pressing a navigation key — and routes processing accordingly to display, look up, or navigate away from a credit card transaction's full details.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-ENTER-KEY
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles the operator's request to look up a specific credit card transaction by its Transaction ID. It validates that an ID has been entered, retrieves the full transaction record from the master file, and displays all associated details on screen.

paragraphs.name: RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles the navigation logic when the user exits the transaction detail screen, returning them to whichever screen they came from — or to the sign-on screen if no prior navigation context exists. It packages the current program identity into the shared communication area before handing control to the destination screen.

paragraphs.name: SEND-TRNVIEW-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph assembles and renders the full transaction detail screen to the bank operator or customer service representative. It ensures the screen header is current, carries any error or status message into the display, and presents all retrieved transaction information (or error feedback) to the user.

paragraphs.name: RECEIVE-TRNVIEW-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph captures the input submitted by the bank operator or customer service representative from the transaction detail screen, collecting any Transaction ID entered or navigation key pressed. It is the entry point for processing the user's interaction with the transaction view form.

paragraphs.name: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO
paragraphs.description: This paragraph prepares the standard header information displayed at the top of the transaction detail screen, including the application titles, current date and time, and the identity of the active program. It ensures every screen presentation is consistently stamped with contextual metadata so the bank operator knows exactly when they are viewing the information and within which application module.

paragraphs.name: READ-TRANSACT-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves the full details of a specific credit card transaction from the master transaction file using the Transaction ID entered by the operator. It handles all possible outcomes — successful retrieval, transaction not found, or an unexpected system error — and responds appropriately to each.

paragraphs.name: CLEAR-CURRENT-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles the PF4 key action, resetting the transaction detail screen to a blank state so the operator can start a fresh lookup without any previously displayed transaction data remaining visible.

paragraphs.name: INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph resets the transaction detail screen to a completely blank state, clearing all previously displayed transaction information and any status messages. It prepares a clean slate before a new transaction lookup is performed or when the screen needs to be refreshed.
